text.p: Following are the highlights of main stories in Serbian and Montenegrin papers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
POLITIKA
- Greece supports Yugoslavia's full integration in Europe and international organisations, said Greek foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos during a visit by his Yugoslav counterpart Milan Milutinovic.
- Germany is ready in principle to support Yugoslavia's admission to the international coummunity and its institutions, said German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel.

- Slovenia will appeal the Cyprus court decision of not being competent to rule in its suit against Serbia's bank Beogradska banka offshore office in Cyprus. Slovenia claims $146 million of the bank's assets.
- Two Serbs were killed on August 8 in Marinci village in U.N.-controlled Eastern Slavonia, the head of the regional transition police force Ivan Babic said.

- Main goal of the country's monetary policy in the second half of 1997 will remain maintaining dinar and price stability, banking committee of the Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce said. It warned about shortage of working capital which affects revival of production.
- Serbian Development fund granted 54 million German marks of credits to agricultural firms and cooperatives.
- Investments in agriculture this year will be some 400 million German marks. The sector is expected to grow five to six percent in 1997 over 1996, says Serbia's ruling Socialist Party (SPS).

- The Democratic Party of Socialists of Montenegro (DPS) wing led by prime minister Milo Djukanovic appealed to the constitutional court over decision to accept the presidential candidacy of Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic.
- Bulatovic's DPS wing will continue its congress on Saturday in Podgorica.
NASA BORBA
- The EU will not take a stand on the plan of some opposition parties in Serbia to boycott the upcoming elections considering this to be internal party policy.
- The People's Party (NS), which joined the Democratic Party in 1995, says DS decision to boycott upcoming elections is violating the two parties' unification agreement.

- Serbian Renewal Movement (SPO) says opening of state television to all parties which will take part in elections and presence of OSCE monitors are conditions for SPO participation in the upcoming elections.
- Some 55 percent of 1,007 pollees have not decided who they will vote for in Serbia's elections, according to a poll by Argument agency.

- France's car maker Peugeot has decided not to form a joint venture with Serbia's Zastava after several months of talks. Main reason believed to be unstable political and economic situation in the country.
- U.S. television company S-TA and Russian media concern Medija-Most will compete for the purchase of 49 percent stake in Belgrade television Studio B, Moscow media report.
BORBA
- Italian tourist association Itineraria to organise hunting trips to Yugoslavia in cooperation with Belgrade's Lovoturs and Srbijasume.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Democratic Party accused the federal government of dragging its feet over import of ten Mercedes buses that Berlin has given to Belgrade.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA

- Montenegrin Parliament Speaker Svetozar Marovic said prime minister Milo Djukanovic can be the sole candidate of the Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) in the presidential elections. Marovic criticised the decision of the Republican Election Commission approving Momir Bulatovic's nomination as the second DPS candidate as illegal.
- Leader of the People's Party (NS) of Montenegro Novak Kilibarda said the opposition should nominate a single candidate in the presidential election race.
- The Development Secretariat rejected allegations of the head of the DPS parliament group Predrag Bulatovic that its computer department can forge the next presidential elections.
- Over 10,000 Russian tourists will vacation in Montenegro this year. Aeroflot opened a weekly charter line between Moscow and Tivat this week. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
